Texts.Text: Hello, this is a demonstration of my dialogue asset for Unity. My name is Cerff :)

This system was made to be as simple as possible, and it is completely modular. Feel free to tinker with the source code and modify it as you wish. I would also love to receive PRs with your features, if applicable. The repository for this project is public.
Normally, I would make a devlog to explain everything, but why not use the plugin itself for that? Later, I will publish it on Itch.io as a portfolio — stonks.
So, choose one of the questions below, and I will be happy to answer:

Texts.Text: Well, let me demonstrate some interesting features:
The first thing you might have noticed is the change of emotions of my character.

But you also noticed the speed control? :spd(5)See, I can talk extremely :spd(65)fast, or very slowly. :spd(25)This helps to give more immersion in dialogues. One example of a game that uses this is :dec(bold)Undertale:dec(nbold). But that’s not all...
I’m using Unity’s TextMesh Pro, so it is totally possible to add :col(red)colors:col(white), animations, and much more to the text.

Of course, since this is just a demo, I haven’t added all these features. But it’s quite simple to implement them: just create a tag in the XML, like :red), associate an action in the reading script, and then execute that action in the text writing script.
All this I talked about is explained in more detail in the asset documentation. I strongly recommend reading this document before starting to use the system, at least up to the usage instructions.

Texts.Text: Glad you asked. I like to explain the system through three layers: Data, Integration, and Front-end (any resemblance to MVC is purely coincidental).

The Data layer consists of XML files, where all dialogues are stored. I wrote them manually but have tested with some AIs like Copilot, which can generate the XMLs (with certain limitations). I plan to develop a dialogue creation script in the future.
The Integration layer is responsible for reading the data layer files and preparing them for presentation in the front-end. This is where I implement text speed and other features.
Finally, the Front-end handles presentation and user interaction. It’s everything configured by the Unity editor, basically.

I only ask that you notify me if you use it. It’s just so I know how many projects are using my system :)
